headline: The UK medicines regulator, the MHRA, has published a 2030 strategy that says it must change how it regulates in an era of AI and personalised medicines.
score_reason: Official publication by the national medicines and devices regulator; stands at the bottom of the 7 band because the AI detail is thin.
importance_line: It signals how the UK will approve medicines and medical technology, including AI-based ones, affecting patients and drug and device makers, though the page gives goals more than concrete AI rules.
summary: The MHRA, the UK regulator of medicines and medical devices, says in its 2030 Strategy, published on 14 Oct 2026, that it will aim to give patients faster access to safe treatments and keep pace with advances in AI, data and personalised medicine across all four UK nations. It also promises more patient-centred regulation, a Women's Health Plan and a tougher line on illegal medicines; the strategy states aims and has not yet shown results.
notes: Official government page; the quoted praise comes from industry and the HRA, not independent assessment. The page text we got gives few AI specifics.
